Built for this platform

What you can do with Apple Ads MCP

01

Review App Store acquisition

Ask your agent for campaign reports over an explicit period. Compare spend and the acquisition metrics Apple returns, with their original definitions intact.

02

Inspect campaigns before acting

Read the campaign details behind a result: status, budget, and the account it belongs to. Use those details to explain a recommendation rather than relying on a screenshot.

03

Make deliberate budget changes

Preview a daily budget or campaign-status change through Adport’s policy engine. The local preview is separate from Apple accepting the final API request.

Know what the data means

Apple Ads is also searched for as Apple Search Ads. This connector manages advertising data, not App Store Connect app submissions, reviews, or subscription analytics.

Local setup · Bring your own credentials

Connect Apple Ads to Claude Code or Cursor.

The npm CLI and MCP server run on your machine. You need Node.js 22.13 or newer, your own provider credentials, and permission to access the ad account.

01 Install Adport

npm install -g adport

02 Connect Apple Ads

adport connect apple

The local wizard uses API-user credentials and a private-key file on your machine. This differs from the future managed Cloud connection, which uses browser authorization.

03 Check your connection

adport doctor
adport accounts --provider apple

Check that the intended account appears before asking your agent to report on it. Never paste tokens, client secrets, or private keys into chat.

Before you connect

  • An Apple Ads account and an API user with the role required for your use case.
  • An EC key pair generated locally. Upload only the public key to Apple Ads.
  • The client ID, team ID, key ID, and local path to the private-key file. Never paste the private key into your AI conversation.
Full Apple Ads connection guideOfficial Apple Ads API documentation

Adport is independent and is not endorsed by Apple Ads. Provider access and approval are separate from installing this package.

Use Apple Ads from your agent.

Apple Ads in Claude Code

After connecting locally, register Adport as a stdio MCP server:

claude mcp add --transport stdio adport -- adport mcp

Start a new session and ask Claude to list your connected Apple Ads accounts.

Claude Code MCP documentation

Apple Ads in Cursor

Add this entry to your Cursor MCP configuration. Merge it with existing servers rather than replacing them:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "adport": {
      "command": "adport",
      "args": [
        "mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}

The command must be available on Cursor’s PATH. Enable the server and ask the agent to inspect your account.

You stay in control

A suggestion is not a live change.

The first mutation call returns a preview and a short-lived pending-operation token. Applying requires that token and the same arguments. Budget caps and protected accounts are checked by the policy engine; new campaigns are paused by policy.

Local operations are recorded in an append-only audit log. An approved preview is not a guarantee of provider acceptance, and a connected agent does not grant additional account permissions.

Apple Ads MCP questions

Do I need to send Adport my Apple private key?

Not for local use. The CLI reads the private-key file on your machine to authenticate as your Apple Ads API user. Upload only the public key to Apple, and keep secrets out of chat and source control.

Can I use Apple Ads locally without Adport Cloud?

Yes. Install Adport from npm, connect your own Apple Ads credentials, and register the local MCP server with a stdio-compatible agent such as Claude Code or Cursor. Your provider may have its own approval, access, or billing requirements.

Why can I connect an account but not read a report or apply a change?

Account discovery, reporting, and mutations can require different permissions. Check the requested account, provider app scopes, advertiser eligibility, and environment. Start with adport doctor and the connection guide above. Do not bypass a denied operation by sharing secrets with the agent.
